unit_economics.note: Hero block is the August model (evidence based). Per SKU rows are the bottom up H2 cost base at the active duty scenario (Copper) and FX 1430; air freight for launch lots.

sensitivity.note: Live formulas (compact one line P&L applied to the Monthly and Annual tabs). Factory cost Alibaba case = midpoint of the $17 to $22 benchmark with duty on the higher FOB.

levers.model_cell: Landed Cost & Tariff Scenarios: Medium row, Copper vs Fiber
levers.effect_basis: 18 month net: (copper landed % minus fiber landed %) times Medium 18 month revenue

levers.lever: Air to ocean freight after the Day 90 gate
levers.model_cell: SKU Unit Economics constants: air and ocean per kg; Assumptions: landed COGS change Year 2
levers.effect_basis: 18 month net, upper bound: (air minus ocean freight per hero unit) times 18 month units; the model phases the switch in from the ocean start month through the Year 2 landed change

levers.model_cell: Assumptions: returns % Year 1 and Year 2 onward (Medium)
levers.effect_basis: 18 month net: the returns point saved times 18 month revenue

levers.model_cell: Assumptions: ad spend % by phase; Sensitivity: ad spend minus 3 points
levers.effect_basis: 18 month net: 2 points of ad spend times 18 month revenue

levers.lever: Review velocity (Vine, insert card, Brand Registry follow up)
levers.effect_basis: 18 month net: 10% more units at the same contribution per unit after advertising; fixed costs unchanged

levers.lever: Length variations under one parent ASIN
levers.model_cell: Not a numeric driver; supports levers 4 and 5
levers.effect_basis: Supports levers 4 and 5 (shared reviews and ad budget across the lengths)

levers.model_cell: SKU Unit Economics: H2 cost KRW; Sensitivity: factory cost minus 10%
levers.effect_basis: 18 month net: FOB minus 5% with the duty on that FOB saved too, through the hero FOB share of price

levers.lever: Packaging to a smaller FBA size tier
levers.model_cell: Assumptions: FBA fee per unit (hero basis); SKU tab FBA fee column
levers.effect_basis: 18 month net, upper bound: the FBA fee saving per unit times 18 month units (applies to the 7M and 10M lengths only)

levers.lever: 3PL feeding FBA, avoid aged inventory surcharges
levers.effect_basis: 18 month net: half a point of storage and inbound times 18 month revenue

levers.lever: Price ladder and coupons (list vs sale price)
levers.model_cell: Assumptions: ASP Years 1 and 2; Sensitivity: ASP plus or minus 10%
levers.effect_basis: 18 month net: plus 5% ASP with every percentage cost scaling with revenue (minus 5% costs the same amount)

levers.lever: Off Amazon email list (Spec Match finder, trade up registration)

model_notes.where: Assumptions: Ad spend % Months 13 to 18 and Months 19 to 24
model_notes.default: Months 13 to 18 at Low 18%, Medium 11%, High 8%; Months 19 to 24 at Low 18%, Medium 11%, High 9.5%
model_notes.why: The brief's floor (ad spend never below 8% of revenue) is applied at the company level across all channels. With High at 8% on Amazon only, the eBay and Walmart (5%) and B2B (3%) mix diluted Year 2 to 7.4%. High steps to its Year 3 rate from Month 19, which keeps the 18 month block exactly as the August model and lifts High Year 2 to 8.1%.

model_notes.default: The workbook High 18 month net is $447K (24.2%). The spec sentence said $457,804 (24.7%), which needs 7% ads in Months 13 to 18, below the 8% floor; the brief says $455K (24.6%). The workbook is 1.7% from the brief, inside the 2% tolerance.
model_notes.why: The 8% floor wins over the spec figure. Decks quote $447K and 24.2% from figures.json, never $457,804 or $455K.

model_notes.default: Low lost quarter in Months 19 to 21 at 10% of trend (spec 2.5 said Months 15 to 17)
model_notes.why: Spec 2.3 also requires the Low 18 month block to reproduce the brief's $633K revenue and ($19K) net, which a Months 15 to 17 suppression (about $169K of revenue) makes impossible. The brief only requires one lost quarter in Low. Do not move it back without re calibrating the Low 18 month block.

model_notes.where: Scenario Summary: Low Year 2 and Year 3 net margin
model_notes.default: Low net margin rises from Year 2 to Year 3
model_notes.why: Year 2 carries the lost quarter (Months 19 to 21), so the Year 2 to Year 3 step is a recovery, not better economics. From Year 3 the Low margin compresses every year and Year 5 net is at or below zero.

model_notes.default: Low 135, Medium 95, High 85 days of landed COGS (spec 2.6 started at 90, 75, 60)
model_notes.why: Raised to the days implied by the Month 24 stock (cover months plus one lead time in transit) so Year 3 does not release cash artificially. Only the Year 3 to 5 balances change; peak need and funding gap sit in Months 7 to 24 in every scenario.

model_notes.where: Assumptions rows for ASP change, ad spend Years 3 to 5, landed change Years 3 to 5, Low unit growth
model_notes.default: Medium ASP change -4% per year (spec minus 2%); Medium ad spend Years 3 to 5 11.5% flat (spec 9.5, 9.0, 8.5); Medium landed change Y3 -1.5, Y4 -1.0, Y5 -0.5 points (spec minus 2.5, minus 2.0, minus 1.5); Low ad spend Years 3 to 5 13%, 13.5%, 16.5% (spec 12 flat); High ad spend 9.5% flat (spec 9.0, 8.5, 8.0); High ASP change -3% (spec minus 1.5%); Low unit growth 10%, 8%, 5% (spec 5, 3, 0; within the plus or minus 5 bound)
model_notes.why: The Year 5 bands are reached with heavier price and ad compression than the spec started from, so that margin compresses at least 1 point a year (brief realism rule) and the Low case stalls near $1M with a non positive Year 5 net. Every row carries a Note on Assumptions.

model_notes.default: Medium -1.0 points (spec minus 2.0; fix round 1 used minus 1.5)
model_notes.why: Creep back starts in Year 4 so the Medium net margin step from Year 3 to Year 4 exceeds 1 point (it was 0.96).

model_notes.default: 2.0% in every scenario (spec 2.5 channel economics said 1.5%)
model_notes.why: The brief's realism rule (returns never below 2%) wins. The pro line B2B share inherits the same rate. Costs about $4K of Medium Year 5 net.

Spec 2.5 asks for a Low Year 5 net that is negative or near zero. At 14% the Low Year 5 net was about $14K positive; at this rate it is at or below zero while cash before funding stays negative at every year end and the Month 12 gate reads KILL.

model_notes.default: Form 5472 preparation, the Wyoming report, the bond renewal and the product liability premium are charged from the Year 2 start month (Month 19); Year 1 sits inside the August $850 per month fixed cost and the $9,500 launch costs
model_notes.why: Keeps the 18 month reconciliation exact. It understates Months 4 to 18 by at most about $1,500. The compliance calendar must still trigger the $1M product liability policy in the first month sales pass $10K (Medium Month 4).

model_notes.where: Levers tab and Plan B tab
model_notes.default: Both read the Medium column of Assumptions, not the Active column
model_notes.why: Spec 2.8 quotes Medium From and To values and spec 2.7 defines Plan B as a fixed side case; pinning them means the lever table and Plan B read the same whatever the selector shows. No P&L, cash or gate figure depends on them. The landed % on Plan B still follows the duty and FX selectors.

model_notes.default: Gate results are PASS, REVIEW or KILL
model_notes.why: Spec 2.7 defines PASS and KILL only. REVIEW (no kill trigger fired, but not every pass threshold met) means fix and retest within 30 days. Low reads REVIEW at Day 90 and KILL at Month 12.

model_notes.where: Cash Flow and Working Capital: Low peak need
model_notes.default: The order rule keeps buying through the Low lost quarter to rebuild cover for the recovery month
model_notes.why: The Low peak need at Month 24 therefore assumes purchases continue during the suppression. An operator would pause orders until the listing is restored; the modeled figure is conservative.

model_notes.default: Runway after funding = cash after the funding draw divided by the Months 4 to 6 burn; the draw is 1.2 times the peak need
model_notes.why: A more profitable case with a smaller draw can show a shorter runway. If the Day 90 runway test is marginal, size the line at the larger of the funding gap and four months of burn.
Spec 3 asks for Landed Cost and Tariff Scenarios (32 characters) but Excel caps sheet names at 31. The tab's A1 title carries the full wording. No number is affected.

day90.metric: Unit session conversion on at least 3 of the 5 launch SKUs
TACOS in Month 3, falling month over month
Contribution per unit before advertising on at least 3 of 5 SKUs
Cash runway after funding the next purchase order

month12.kill: three consecutive negative months with a funding gap above $50,000

kill_criteria.kill_means: No further capital, sell down inventory, delist losers, move to Plan B

full_recalc.note: Each block is a full LibreOffice recalc of the workbook at the stated selectors (Scenario 2 Medium unless stated). Quote duty and FX effects from here, not from the compact Sensitivity rows.
